about: Check of the app's MEC claims against the Priorización curricular 2021 (1.er y 2.º ciclo): three independent readings of the document, a verdict per claim, and a challenge of each verdict. Pages are PDF pages (printed page = PDF page - 6).

answers.q: Q1. Is the 1st-cycle 'Comunicación Guaraní' table the program for Guarani as L2, L1, or both? What in the document says so?
answers.answer:
The table never labels itself. Its heading is just "Comunicación Guaraní", with no L1, L2, "lengua materna" or "segunda lengua" label (p26). The only marker of the learner type inside the table is in the 3.º grado alcance, which speaks of "imperfecciones propias del proceso de aprendizaje de la L2" (p26). That frames the Guarani table as second-language learning. The table nowhere mentions L1 or lengua materna.

The term "lengua materna" appears instead in the 1st-cycle "Comunicación Castellano" table. All three of its alcances say the children express themselves "utilizando su lengua materna" (p23). That table also has Guarani-specific spelling rules: item 17 includes "La tilde y la marca de nasalidad, en el caso del guaraní" next to rules marked "en el caso del castellano" (p25). The document does not explicitly say that this Castellano table is the program for Guarani-L1 children. That reading is an inference, not something the text states.

Cuadro 4 (1st cycle) names the subjects "Castellano" and "Guaraní". Cuadro 5 (2nd cycle) names them "Lengua Materna" and "Segunda Lengua" and does not say which language is which (p21). Nothing in the document says the Guarani table serves both L1 and L2. Printed page numbers differ from PDF pages: PDF p26 is printed page 20. All citations here use PDF pages.

answers.q: Q2. In 1.º grado, does the Guarani program include reading and writing, or only listening and speaking? Compare the alcance with the capacities.
answers.answer:
The two parts do not match. The 1.º grado alcance is oral only. It speaks of using "vocabulario elemental", keeping up "conversaciones breves" and asking and answering questions, and it never mentions reading or writing (p26).

The list of capacities does include reading and writing:
- Its two blocks are headed "Comprensión oral y escrita" (p26) and "Expresión oral y escrita" (p27).
- Item 1 refers to a text "antes de escucharlo o leerlo".
- Item 2 predicts content "a partir de láminas".
- Items 17, 19, 20 and 21 cover writing: writing cards, riddles, dialogues, descriptions and short narratives; spelling sounds; and applying rules for letters and basic punctuation (p28).

In short, the 1.º grado alcance is oral, but its capacity list has written items.

answers.q: Q3. In which grade does written Guarani first appear in the alcance?
answers.answer: In 2.º grado. Its alcance is the first to say "en forma oral y escrita". The 3.º grado alcance repeats the phrase. The 1.º grado alcance has no written element (p26). In the 2nd cycle, the 4.º grado alcance says "ojehai ha oñehendúva" (written and heard) and "oñe'ẽ ha ohaikuévo" (speaking and writing) (p45).

answers.q: Q4. What does the document say about children whose mother tongue is Guarani: when do they read and write in Guarani?
answers.answer:
Not in the document. No page I read (p18-28, p40-42, p45-47) and no text search of the whole PDF finds a statement about children whose mother tongue is Guarani, or about when they read and write in Guarani. The Guarani table mentions only "L2" (p26).

The closest passages are in the 1st-cycle Castellano table:
- Its 1.º grado alcance speaks of "lectoescritura" and "su lengua materna" (p23).
- Its writing-rule item names "La tilde y la marca de nasalidad, en el caso del guaraní" in 1.º, 2.º and 3.º grado (p25).

The document does not say these apply to Guarani-L1 children. The app's claim "Con el guaraní como lengua materna, en 1.º grado se empieza a leer y escribir" is not stated in the document.

answers.q: Q5. Topics named for 1.º, 2.º and 3.º grado in Guarani.
answers.answer:
**1.º grado** (p26-28):
- Greetings and courtesy (item 4).
- Personal data: nombre, edad y grado (5).
- Instructions: manipulating objects and appliances, placing them, moving from place to place (3).
- Text types heard: trabalenguas, chistes, rimas, poesías, canciones, cuentos, descripciones, fábulas, leyendas, diálogos e instrucciones breves (7).
- Words of the immediate context: "mi cuerpo, mi familia, mi casa, mi escuela y mi país"; words in short poems, songs, descriptions and riddles (10).
- Greetings and introductions (12).
- Dialogues on everyday topics (13).
- Activities during the day: mañana, tarde y noche (14).
- Agreement or disagreement (15).
- Needs: asking for help, a favour, permission, the loan of an object (16).
- Writing: tarjetas, adivinanzas, diálogos, descripciones (personas, paisajes, animales, plantas y objetos) y narraciones breves (17).
- Courtesy expressions (18).
- Spelling and rules for letters and basic punctuation (19-21).

**2.º grado:** the same core, plus:
- "etiquetas" among the texts (7).
- Introducing classmates and family (12).
- Basic needs: "ir al baño, tomar agua, pedir alimentos, solicitar permiso y prestar algo" (16).
- Writing esquelas, poemas and acrósticos, "teniendo en cuenta la estructura de cada tipo de texto" (17).
- Norms for letras, mayúsculas, "la tilde y la marca de nasalidad" (20).

**3.º grado:**
- "noticias breves" among the texts (7).
- Analysing a narrative text: personajes, acciones, lugar y tiempo (11).
- Introducing others with their características, gustos y aficiones (12).
- Wishes and needs in everyday social situations (16).

Topics the document does not name in the 1st-cycle Guarani table include numbers, colours, the alphabet or vowels, food as a topic, and places, directions or asking where something is. Animals appear only as objects of description (item 17), and food only as "pedir alimentos" (2.º, item 16).

answers.q: Q6. Weekly hours of Guarani (regular and 2021) in the 1st and 2nd cycle, and how the 2nd cycle names its language areas.
answers.answer:
**1st cycle (Cuadro 4, p21):**
- Guaraní: 4 hours regular, 3 in the 2021 proposal.
- Castellano: 5 regular, 3 in 2021.
- Comunicación as a whole: 11 regular, 7 in 2021.
- Total: 30 regular, 20 in 2021.

**2nd cycle (Cuadro 5, p21):** there is no row named Guaraní or Castellano. The language areas are "Lengua Materna" (5 actual, 3 in 2021) and "Segunda Lengua" (4 actual, 3 in 2021). The column headers are "CARGA HORARIA ACTUAL" and "PROPUESTA 2021". The document does not say which language is the Lengua Materna or the Segunda Lengua.

The 2nd-cycle capacity tables are headed "Comunicación Castellano" (p41) and "Comunicación Guaraní" (p45). The 4.º grado Castellano alcance says "utilizando la lengua castellana como instrumento de interacción" (p41).

The 2021 hour is defined on p20: 20 pedagogical hours a week, each equivalent to 35 minutes.

answers.q: Q7. For 4.º, 5.º and 6.º grado: the Guarani alcance (Guarani plus Spanish translation) and the main text types or topics.
answers.answer:
The Spanish translations below are mine, not the document's.

**4.º grado alcance (p45).** Translation: "En este grado se espera que los estudiantes lean y sepan comprender textos no muy largos o cortos, escritos y oídos, que tengan palabras de uso frecuente y no difíciles de comprender. Así podrán contar, al hablar y al escribir, sus necesidades y todo lo que ocurre en su comunidad. Aquí los estudiantes todavía pueden cometer pequeños errores y, donde se equivocan, se les debe seguir corrigiendo/enseñando."

**5.º grado alcance (p45).** Translation: "En este grado se espera que los estudiantes empiecen a leer con fluidez y comprendan también textos escritos y no escritos breves, que tengan palabras un poco más difíciles de comprender. Así podrán contar, al hablar y al escribir, sus necesidades, sus sentimientos y todo lo que ocurre a su alrededor y en otros lugares. Aquí todavía pueden cometer pequeños errores y, donde se equivocan, se les debe seguir corrigiendo."

**6.º grado alcance (p45).** Translation: "Aquí se espera que los estudiantes ya lean con buena fluidez y comprendan también textos breves, escritos y oídos, que tengan palabras más difíciles de comprender. Así podrán contar sus necesidades, sentimientos, pensamientos y todo lo que ocurre a su alrededor y en todo lugar. Aquí todavía pueden cometer pequeños errores y, donde se equivocan, se les debe seguir corrigiendo."

**Section headings.** The 2nd-cycle capacities fall under four Guarani headings:
- "Oikumbýta mba'e ohendúva oje'éva ichupe guaraníme": will understand what is said to them in Guarani (items 1-7, p45).
- "Oñe'ẽkuaáta guaraníme": will know how to speak in Guarani (8-13, p46).
- "Oikũmbýta jehaipyre omoñe'ẽva guaraníme": will understand the written texts they read in Guarani (14-19, p46-47).
- "Ohaíta guaraníme": will write in Guarani (20-24, p47).

**Main text types and topics:**
- Oral instructions for games and for how to do things (item 1). In 5.º this includes using household utensils; in 6.º, recipes ("tembi'ukuéra").
- Main ideas (2) and listening to news ("ñe'ẽmondo", 4.º-5.º, item 4).
- Greeting and noticing the context (8).
- Daily activities: morning, afternoon and night (4.º, item 9). In 5.º, what they do at home and school; in 6.º, their own and their family's activities.
- Trabalenguas and poems ("kũjererã ha ñe'ẽpoty"). 5.º and 6.º add songs and more ("purahéi ha hetave mba'e") (11).
- Describing people, animals, places and things (13).
- Reading:
  - 4.º: written dialogues on current topics (14).
  - 5.º: stories or poems ("mombe'urã térã ñe'ẽpoty") on current topics (14).
  - 6.º: all kinds of texts on current topics (14).
  - Written instructions (15).
  - Analysis of text coherence, cohesion and adequacy, and of how a narrative starts and develops (19).
- Writing:
  - Their activities at home and school (20).
  - What they do with family, friends and others (21).
  - Retelling stories read or heard (22).
  - Writing so that the meaning is understood (23).
  - Using signs that help the reader (24).

The 2nd-cycle Guarani table does not name: letters ("cartas"), myths or legends by name, radio or TV news, pronouns, verbs or conjugation, accents, possessives, or the oración. "Leyendas", "noticias y crónicas" and "textos científicos breves" do appear in the 2nd-cycle Castellano table (p42).

answers.q: Q1. Is the 1st-cycle 'Comunicación Guaraní' table the program for Guarani as L2, as L1, or for both? What in the document says so?
answers.answer: The document gives ONE Guarani table per grade (p26-28). It does not show separate L1 and L2 tracks. The only explicit marker is in the 3.º grado alcance, which calls the learning process 'la L2'. That supports reading the table as Guarani as a second language. The document never says in so many words 'this table is for L2 only' or 'for L1 children use X'. There is no Guarani-as-L1 program in the document, and it does not say how the table applies to Guarani-speaking children (not in the document). One qualifying point: the 1st-cycle 'Comunicación Castellano' table is framed around 'lengua materna', and its writing capacities include Guarani spelling rules ('en el caso del guaraní'). So the Castellano table is written so that it can cover either language for some orthography items. The document does not explain this, and I do not infer more. In the 2nd cycle, the hours table names the areas 'Lengua Materna' and 'Segunda Lengua' (p21), but the capacity tables are titled 'Comunicación Castellano' and 'Comunicación Guaraní'. The document never maps one onto the other. SKEPTIC NOTE: the app has three tracks (L1/L2/BI). Their notes ('lee y escribe en guaraní desde 1.º grado' for L1 and BI) are not in this document.

answers.q: Q2. In 1.º grado, does the Guarani program include reading and writing, or only listening and speaking? Compare the alcance with its capacities.
answers.answer: There is a real tension in the document. The 1.º grado ALCANCE is oral only. It says 'utilizar vocabulario elemental', 'mantener conversaciones breves' and 'formular y responder preguntas', and it never says 'escrita'. (Compare the 2.º alcance, which adds 'en forma oral o escrita'.) But the 1.º grado CAPACITIES include reading and writing. The two capacity blocks are headed 'Comprensión oral y escrita' and 'Expresión oral y escrita'. Capacity 1 mentions a text 'antes de escucharlo o leerlo'. Capacity 17 is 'Escribe tarjetas, adivinanzas, diálogos, descripciones ... y narraciones breves'. Capacities 19 and 21 are 'Utiliza la grafía correspondiente para representar sonidos'. Capacity 20 is 'Aplica en sus redacciones las reglas de uso de: Las letras. Los signos básicos de puntuación.' Most of the comprehension capacities (7, 9) refer to texts 'escuchados' only, while 2.º adds 'o leídos'. So the honest reading: the alcance describes an oral outcome, but the prioritized capacities for 1.º already include writing. SKEPTIC NOTE: the app says that with Guarani as L2, '1.º grado es oral' and 'leer y escribir empieza en 2.º grado'. The 1.º alcance supports this, but capacities 17, 19, 20 and 21 contradict it. The claim is too strong as stated.

answers.q: Q3. In which grade does written Guarani first appear in the alcance?
answers.answer: 2.º grado. It is the first Guarani alcance that says 'en forma oral o escrita' and mentions understanding information from texts from sources such as a 'periódico'. The 3.º alcance repeats 'en forma oral y escrita'. The 1.º alcance has no reference to writing or reading. Note, though, that the 1.º CAPACITIES already include writing (see Q2), so 'first appears in the alcance' is not the same as 'first appears in the program'.

answers.q: Q4. What does the document say about children whose mother tongue is Guarani: when do they read and write in Guarani?
answers.answer: Not in the document. No passage says when children whose mother tongue is Guarani read or write in Guarani. The document never names a 'Guarani como lengua materna' program. The only mother-tongue references are these: the 1st-cycle Castellano alcance ('utilizando su lengua materna para comunicarse', 'utilizando la lengua materna en su interacción social'), the Castellano writing capacity about Guarani orthography ('en el caso del guaraní'), and the 2nd-cycle hours table ('Lengua Materna'/'Segunda Lengua'). None of these says that Guarani-L1 children read and write in Guarani in 1.º grado. SKEPTIC NOTE: the app's L1 claim ('lee y escribe en guaraní desde 1.º grado'), its 1.º grado text ('Con el guaraní como lengua materna, en 1.º grado se empieza a leer y escribir') and its 2.º text ('como lengua materna, se afianza') are not supported by this document. If they come from another source (for example Ley 1264/98, art. 31, which the app cites for Preescolar), that source must be cited instead.

answers.q: Q5. Topics named for 1.º, 2.º and 3.º grado in Guarani.
answers.answer: Greetings and courtesy: cap. 4 in all three grades, cap. 12 and cap. 18 in 1.º, and cap. 21 in 2.º. Personal data (nombre, edad y grado): cap. 5, all grades. Immediate context, 'mi cuerpo, mi familia, mi casa, mi escuela y mi país': cap. 10, all grades. The 1.º alcance also names 'datos personales, del hogar y la escuela'. Parts of the day, 'a la mañana, a la tarde y a la noche': cap. 14, all grades. Needs: cap. 16. 1.º has 'pedir ayuda, favor, permiso, préstamo de algún objeto o material'. 2.º has 'ir al baño, tomar agua, pedir alimentos, solicitar permiso y prestar algo'. 3.º has 'deseos y necesidades en situaciones sociales cotidianas'. Instructions: cap. 3, all grades, 'manipular objetos y electrodomésticos, ubicarlos en un lugar determinado y trasladarse de un lugar a otro'. Agreement and disagreement: cap. 15. Texts to understand (cap. 7): in 1.º, 'trabalenguas, chistes, rimas, poesías, canciones, cuentos, descripciones, fábulas, leyendas, diálogos e instrucciones breves'. 2.º adds 'etiquetas'. 3.º adds 'noticias breves'. Texts to write (cap. 17): in 1.º, 'tarjetas, adivinanzas, diálogos, descripciones ... y narraciones breves'. 2.º and 3.º add 'esquelas', 'poemas' and 'acrósticos'. Characters (cap. 9 and 11). In 3.º, narrative analysis: 'personajes, acciones, lugar y tiempo'. Orthography: 1.º has 'Las letras' and 'Los signos básicos de puntuación'. 2.º and 3.º have 'Las letras', 'Las mayúsculas' and 'La tilde y la marca de nasalidad'. SKEPTIC NOTES on app units and 'mec' text. NOT in the Guarani 1st-cycle table: numbers 1 to 10; 'el alfabeto: las vocales y el puso'; the consonant list (ch, mb, nd, ng, nt, rr, g̃); animals or food as unit topics (animals appear only as description objects in cap. 17); 'preguntar por un lugar / dar direcciones'; 'palabras que se escriben igual en castellano y en guaraní'; and, for 3.º, 'reglas de juegos, recetas' and 'ideas principales'. Those last two come from the Castellano table (p23-24), not the Guarani one. The Guarani 3.º grado has 'Secuencia los hechos' (cap. 6) and electrical-appliance instructions (cap. 3). The claim 'se consolidan la lectura y la escritura en las dos lenguas' is not stated for Guarani; the 3.º Guarani alcance still speaks of 'imperfecciones propias del proceso de aprendizaje de la L2'.

answers.q: Q7. For 4.º, 5.º and 6.º grado: the Guarani alcance (Guarani + faithful Spanish translation) and main text types or topics.
answers.answer: 4.º, translated: 'En este grado se espera que los estudiantes lean y sepan comprender textos no muy largos o bastante breves, escritos y escuchados, que tengan palabras de uso frecuente y que no sean difíciles de entender. Así podrán contar, al hablar y al escribir, sus necesidades y todo lo que pasa en su comunidad. Aquí los estudiantes todavía pueden cometer pequeños errores, y donde se equivoquen se les debe corregir/orientar más.' 5.º, translated: 'En este grado se espera que los estudiantes empiecen a leer con fluidez y también sepan comprender textos escritos y no escritos [orales] bastante breves, que tengan palabras algo más difíciles de entender. Así podrán contar, al hablar y al escribir, sus necesidades, sus sentimientos y todo lo que pasa a su alrededor y en otros lugares. Aquí los estudiantes todavía pueden cometer pequeños errores ...' 6.º, translated: 'Aquí se espera que los estudiantes ya lean con buena fluidez y también comprendan textos breves, escritos y escuchados, con palabras más difíciles de entender. Así podrán contar sus necesidades, sentimientos, pensamientos y todo lo que pasa a su alrededor y en todas partes. Aquí los estudiantes todavía pueden cometer pequeños errores ...' The 6.º Guarani literally reads 'ñe'ẽjehaipyre'ỹ ... ojehai ha oñehendúva', which is internally odd ('unwritten texts, written and heard'). The document labels 6.º as closing the cycle only in the Castellano table ('deben lograr el desarrollo íntegro de la competencia del ciclo', p41), not in the Guarani one. The 2nd-cycle Guarani table is organised in four blocks: 'Oikumbýta mba'e ohendúva oje'éva ichupe guaraníme' (listening comprehension), 'Oñe'ẽkuaáta guaraníme' (speaking), 'Oikũmbýta jehaipyre omoñe'ẽva guaraníme' (reading comprehension) and 'Ohaíta guaraníme' (writing). Main topics and text types: instructions for games, household tools and things for their age (and food in 6.º) (cap. 1, 15); what is said about home (4.º), plus school (5.º), plus other matters (6.º) (cap. 2); polysemous words (cap. 5); respecting others' opinions (cap. 7); greetings suited to the interlocutor (cap. 8); daily activities at home and school and with family and friends (cap. 9, 20, 21); 'kũjererã' (trabalenguas) and 'ñe'ẽpoty' (poems), plus 'purahéi' (songs) in 5.º and 6.º (cap. 11); expressive reading (cap. 13); dialogues (4.º) and narratives or poems (5.º) on current topics (cap. 14); text features such as sequence, connectors, purpose, beginning and development, and signs (cap. 16 and 19); retelling in writing 'mombe'urã' (stories), and in 5.º and 6.º 'ñe'ẽpoty ha mombe'ugua'u' (poems and legends) (cap. 22); writing clearly (cap. 23); signs that help the reader (cap. 24); and characters in heard texts in 6.º (cap. 3). SKEPTIC NOTES: these are not in the 2nd-cycle Guarani table: letters and esquelas ('Kuatiañe'ẽ', 4.º); 'la oración y el verbo', 'posesivos', 'acento', 'pronombres', 'conjugar el verbo'; 'mitos' ('mombe'ugua'u' = legends appears, 'mitos' does not); 'noticias de la radio y la tele' (6.º; 'noticias breves' appears only in the 1st-cycle 3.º table); and 'leer entre líneas / deduce lo que un texto no dice'. The app's 2nd-cycle 'mec' phrase 'textos ... para situaciones de todos los días y también formales' is not worded this way in the Guarani alcance.

answers.q: Q1. Is the 1st-cycle 'Comunicación Guaraní' table the program for Guarani as L2, as L1, or both? What in the document says so?
answers.answer: There is only one 'Comunicación Guaraní' table for the 1st cycle (PDF p26-28). The document has no separate Guarani-as-mother-tongue (L1) table and no note that adapts it for L1 or bilingual children. The only track marker in the table is in the 3.º grado alcance, which describes the learner's errors as 'propias del proceso de aprendizaje de la L2' (p26). In the same cycle, the Castellano table's alcance says the child communicates 'utilizando su lengua materna' (p23). Read together, the 1st-cycle document assumes Castellano is the mother tongue and Guarani the second language. It never says this outright, for example in a heading like 'Guaraní como segunda lengua', and it never mentions a child whose mother tongue is Guarani. No passage in the legal-framework pages (p15-17) or the plan of study (p20-21) assigns L1 or L2 to a particular language. The legal pages quote Ley 1264/98 arts. 3, 5, 11, 117 and 125 only. Art. 31 (on mother-tongue teaching, which the app cites for Preescolar) is not quoted anywhere in the document, so the app's art. 31 claim is not in the document. Answer: the document gives the table as the program for every child, and its only L1/L2 wording frames Guarani as L2. That the same table is the L1 or bilingual program is not in the document.

answers.q: Q2. In 1.º grado, does the Guarani program include reading and writing, or only listening and speaking? Compare the alcance with the capacities.
answers.answer: The two parts disagree. The 1.º grado alcance is oral only. It speaks of 'vocabulario elemental', 'conversaciones breves' and asking and answering questions, and unlike 2.º and 3.º it does not say 'en forma oral y escrita'. The capacity list for 1.º, however, falls under the headings 'Comprensión oral y escrita' and 'Expresión oral y escrita', and it includes reading and writing. Cap. 1 anticipates a text 'antes de escucharlo o leerlo'. Cap. 17 'Escribe tarjetas, adivinanzas, diálogos, descripciones ... y narraciones breves'. Cap. 19 and 21 'Utiliza la grafía correspondiente para representar sonidos'. Cap. 20 applies spelling rules ('Las letras', 'Los signos básicos de puntuación'). The reading capacities in 1.º are lighter than in 2.º. Cap. 7 speaks of 'textos breves escuchados', where 2.º says 'escuchados o leídos', and cap. 9 speaks of 'textos escuchados'. So the app's L2 note, that in 1.º the child listens and speaks and starts reading and writing in 2.º, matches the alcance but not the capacity list, which already has writing in 1.º. The document makes no distinction by home language.

answers.q: Q4. What does the document say about children whose mother tongue is Guarani: when do they read and write in Guarani?
answers.answer: Not in the document. Nothing addresses children whose mother tongue is Guarani, or children with both languages at home. The phrase 'lengua materna' appears only in the 1st-cycle Castellano alcance (p23) and as an unassigned area name in Cuadro 5 (p21). 'L2' appears only in the 3.º grado Guarani alcance (p26). The words 'bilingüe'/'Bilingüe' appear only for unrelated programs: indigenous radio classes (p14) and adult basic education (p8, p10). So the app's L1 note ('lee y escribe en guaraní desde 1.º grado') and its BI note ('escucha, habla, lee y escribe en guaraní desde 1.º grado') are not supported by this document. The 1.º grado capacity list (writing in cap. 17, 19, 20, 21) applies to all children equally (see Q2).

answers.q: Q5. Topics named for 1.º, 2.º and 3.º grado in Guarani.
answers.answer: All three grades share the same topics, with small changes by grade. Greetings and courtesy (cap. 4, 12, 18). Personal data: nombre, edad y grado (cap. 5). Vocabulary of the immediate context: mi cuerpo, mi familia, mi casa, mi escuela y mi país (cap. 10). Following brief instructions to handle objects and household appliances and to move from place to place (cap. 3). Activities in the parts of the day: mañana, tarde, noche (cap. 14). Basic needs (cap. 16), which in 1.º are ayuda, favor, permiso, préstamo and in 2.º are ir al baño, tomar agua, pedir alimentos, solicitar permiso y prestar algo. Agreement and disagreement (cap. 15). Text types: in 1.º, trabalenguas, chistes, rimas, poesías, canciones, cuentos, descripciones, fábulas, leyendas, diálogos e instrucciones breves. 2.º adds etiquetas, and 3.º adds noticias breves. The written texts are tarjetas, adivinanzas, diálogos, descripciones y narraciones breves in 1.º, plus esquelas, poemas y acrósticos in 2.º and 3.º. Spelling covers letras and signos básicos de puntuación in 1.º, and letras, mayúsculas, la tilde y la marca de nasalidad in 2.º and 3.º. In 3.º, the child analyzes a narrative text by 'personajes, acciones, lugar y tiempo' and presents others 'mencionando sus características, gustos y aficiones'. Several app topics are not in the Guarani 1st-cycle table and are 'not in the document'. They are: numbers 1-10, the alphabet with vowels and puso, 2.º 'preguntar por un lugar / dar direcciones', 'palabras que se escriben igual en castellano y en guaraní', and 3.º 'reglas de juegos, recetas'. The 3.º 'ideas principales' come from the Castellano table (p23), not the Guarani one. Recipes appear only in the 6.º Guarani table (cap. 1 and 15, 'tembi’u').

answers.q: Q6. Weekly hours of Guarani (regular and 2021) in 1st and 2nd cycle, and how the 2nd cycle names its language areas.
answers.answer: 1st cycle (Cuadro 4, p21): Guaraní 4 regular and 3 in 2021; Castellano 5 regular and 3 in 2021. Both sit under the area 'Comunicación' (11 regular, 7 in 2021). The weekly total is 30 regular and 20 in 2021. 2nd cycle (Cuadro 5, p21): this table has no 'Guaraní' or 'Castellano' rows. The language areas are named 'Lengua Materna' (5 current, 3 in 2021) and 'Segunda Lengua' (4 current, 3 in 2021). The document does not say which of Castellano or Guarani is 'Lengua Materna' or 'Segunda Lengua'. The 2nd-cycle capacity tables are headed 'Comunicación Castellano' (p41) and 'Comunicación Guaraní' (p45), not L1/L2. The 2021 class period is 35 minutes (p20).

answers.q: Q7. 4.º, 5.º, 6.º grado: Guarani alcance (Guarani + Spanish translation) and main text types/topics.
answers.answer: Spanish translations are mine. 4.º: 'En este grado se espera que los estudiantes lean y comprendan textos no muy largos o no muy cortos, escritos y oídos, que contengan palabras de uso frecuente y no difíciles de comprender. Así podrán contar, al hablar y al escribir, sus necesidades y todo lo que ocurre en su comunidad. Aquí los estudiantes todavía pueden cometer pequeños errores, y donde se equivocan se les debe orientar más.' 5.º: 'En este grado se espera que los estudiantes comiencen a leer con fluidez y comprendan también textos escritos y no escritos (orales) no muy cortos, con palabras algo más difíciles de comprender. Así podrán contar, al hablar y al escribir, sus necesidades, sus sentimientos y todo lo que ocurre a su alrededor y en otros lugares. Aquí los estudiantes todavía pueden cometer pequeños errores...' (the same last sentence). 6.º: 'Aquí se espera que los estudiantes ya lean con buena fluidez y comprendan también textos no muy cortos, escritos y oídos, con palabras más difíciles de comprender. Así podrán contar sus necesidades, sentimientos, pensamientos y todo lo que ocurre a su alrededor y en todas partes. Aquí los estudiantes todavía pueden cometer pequeños errores...' All three grades keep the clause that the student may still make small errors ('ojavymimi'). This echoes the L2 framing of 1st-cycle 3.º (p26), though the 2nd-cycle table never says 'L2'. Main text types and topics. 4.º: oral instructions for playing and doing things suited to their age; talk about the home; greetings by place and person; kũjererã (trabalenguas) and ñe’ẽpoty (poesía); written ñemongeta (diálogos) on current topics; written instructions; text cohesion; writing about the activities of the morning, afternoon and night and what they do with the family; retelling mombe’urã (relatos). 5.º: instructions for playing and for using household tools; home and school; kũjererã, ñe’ẽpoty, purahéi (canciones); mombe’urã or ñe’ẽpoty on current topics; retelling mombe’urã, ñe’ẽpoty and mombe’ugua’u (leyendas); writing about home and school, family and friends. 6.º: instructions including cooking food (tembi’u); home, school and other places; opáichagua jehaipyre (all kinds of texts) on current topics; kũjererã, ñe’ẽpoty, purahéi; retelling mombe’urã, ñe’ẽpoty, mombe’ugua’u; inference ('he’iha pe oñeha’ãrõva ichugui'); writing about home, school and everywhere, family, friends and acquaintances. Several app topics are not in the 2nd-cycle Guarani table: cartas y esquelas, la oración y el verbo, mitos, acentos, posesivos, noticias de radio/tele, pronombres, conjugación. 'Ombojoavy umi mba’e haihára he’íva oikovaramoguáicha ha umi he’íva ha’e oimo’ãháicha' (cap. 18) means distinguishing facts from the author's opinions.

claims.current: En casa se habla más guaraní: lee y escribe en guaraní desde 1.º grado.
claims.evidence: Not in the document. No passage speaks of children whose home language is Guarani, and the term «L1» never appears (full-text search). The 1st cycle has one «Comunicación Guaraní» table (p26-28). Its only learner marker frames it as second-language learning: «Podrían seguir apareciendo imperfecciones propias del proceso de aprendizaje de la L2, como parte del desarrollo de la competencia comunicativa.» (3.º alcance, p26). That same table already has writing in 1.º for every pupil, with no home-language condition: «Escribe tarjetas, adivinanzas, diálogos, descripciones (de personas, paisajes, animales, plantas y objetos) y narraciones breves.» (item 17, p28). So the note is not contradicted. «lengua materna» appears only in the Castellano alcances, «se expresen en forma oral y escrita utilizando su lengua materna para comunicarse» (p23), and as the unassigned area «Lengua Materna» in Cuadro 5 (p21). The Castellano 1.º spelling item includes «La tilde y la marca de nasalidad, en el caso del guaraní.» (item 17, p25). The document never says that table is the program for Guarani-speaking children; reading it that way would be inference.
claims.fix: En casa se habla más guaraní: lee y escribe en guaraní desde 1.º grado.

claims.current: En casa se habla más castellano: en 1.º grado escucha y habla guaraní; a leerlo y escribirlo empieza en 2.º grado.
claims.evidence: Matching this track to the Guarani table fits the document, whose only learner marker is «propias del proceso de aprendizaje de la L2» (p26). The 1.º alcance is oral only: «Al culminar el grado, se espera que los estudiantes puedan utilizar vocabulario elemental relacionado con datos personales, del hogar y la escuela, mantener conversaciones breves aplicando funciones comunicativas básicas, con las cuales podrá formular y responder preguntas.» (p26). The 2.º alcance is the first to say «utilizar en forma oral y escrita, vocabulario básico» (p26). One reader quoted «oral o escrita»; the page image reads «oral y escrita». However, the 1.º capacities already include reading and writing. Item 1: «Anticipa posibles informaciones contenidas en un texto antes de escucharlo o leerlo» (p26). Item 17: «Escribe tarjetas, adivinanzas, diálogos, descripciones (de personas, paisajes, animales, plantas y objetos) y narraciones breves.» (p28). Items 19 and 21: «Utiliza la grafía correspondiente para representar sonidos.» (p28). Item 20: «Aplica en sus redacciones las reglas de uso de: • Las letras. • Los signos básicos de puntuación.» (p28). So «empieza en 2.º grado» matches the alcance but not the 1.º capacities.
claims.fix: En casa se habla más castellano: en 1.º grado sobre todo escucha y habla guaraní, y empieza a escribir; desde 2.º grado lee y escribe más.
